subject.title: [OAuth] Client ID revoked `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` - fresh ChatGPT Plus logins completely broken

question: Should OpenClaw rotate or override the built-in OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex OAuth client ID now, and if so should that rotation follow upstream Codex or use an OpenClaw-owned OAuth application?
rationale: This cannot be safely resolved by code inspection alone because client registration, revocation status, app ownership, and browser/device-code parity are controlled outside the repository.

options.title: Verify and coordinate rotation
options.body: Use a maintainer-controlled fresh ChatGPT Plus/Pro login to confirm the browser failure, then rotate the client ID or adopt the upstream-approved override with coverage for browser, device-code, token exchange, and refresh.

options.title: Document temporary recovery only
options.body: If device-code or API-key auth is still acceptable as a stopgap, publish a temporary recovery path while leaving the built-in browser client unchanged until upstream confirms the revocation.

options.title: Close after upstream disproves it
options.body: If OpenAI/Codex confirms the client is valid and a fresh browser login works outside this worker, close this as not reproduced with exact proof.

recommendation.title: Verify and coordinate rotation
recommendation.body: Use a maintainer-controlled fresh ChatGPT Plus/Pro login to confirm the browser failure, then rotate the client ID or adopt the upstream-approved override with coverage for browser, device-code, token exchange, and refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main and merged-history signals for the OpenAI provider identity and ChatGPT OAuth files point to steipete.
